newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices continue climb with heat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices continue climb with heat.

text.p: U.S. spot gas prices rose further Thursday amid heavy buying following Hurricane Danny last week and near 100 degree F heat in Texas and the southern plains, market sources said.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, physical prices rose about four cents to about $2.24 per mmBtu at Henry Hub.
In south Texas, prices similarly edged four cents higher to about $2.16-2.18 as the thermometer nearly touched 100 degrees F.
The hot weather is forecast to continue through Sunday but then moderate beginning Monday to about 95 degrees F in Dallas, according to a Texas trader.
In the Permian Basin market, prices jumped another 10 cents to about $2.20-2.21.
"I think the Permian jump was 100 percent attributable to California buying," a trader said.
Southern California border prices were up about three cents to the low-$2.30s.
San Juan prices were also higher around $2.18-2.19.
In the Midwest, prices gained another six cents to $2.14-2.16, with Chicago city-gate gas up around $2.33.
In the East, swing gas at the New York city gate prices were also quoted a bit higher at $2.40-2.44 at M3 and Zone 6 despite the significantly cooler weather in the region.
